sermon.title: A Sword
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that Jesus does not spread the gospel by physical force: he pardons sinners, tells Peter to put up the sword, rebukes calling fire on Samaritans, and gives the word as our sword. Civil rulers bear the civil sword; the church preaches repentance and righteousness, including against violent Islam.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Sensitive: Islam/Muslims waging war; adultery pardon. Kept as spoken.

faqs.question: Is a physical gun the same as the gospel’s sword?
faqs.answer: He opens with a gun image to contrast—gospel is not forcing belief with weapons.

faqs.question: Did Jesus have the right to condemn the adulterous woman?
faqs.answer: Yes, because he was without sin—yet he pardoned her.

faqs.question: Does pardon mean the world should promote sin as okay?
faqs.answer: No—he says the world wants to promote sin; Jesus still calls it wrong while offering pardon.

faqs.question: Why were disciples confused when told to put the sword up?
faqs.answer: They thought of force and kingship; that is not what Jesus came to do.

faqs.question: What did Jesus say about the disciples’ spirit wanting fire?
faqs.answer: You know not what manner of spirit you are of—they had the wrong spirit.

faqs.question: Were the apostles first sent only to Israel?
faqs.answer: He says go first to the children of Israel, not to the Gentiles (at that stage).

faqs.question: Does Jesus bring peace or division?
faqs.answer: Peace if you accept his message; division if you refuse—both texts stand.

faqs.question: Can you further the gospel by killing people?
faqs.answer: No—when you kill someone you cannot change them; the word is the weapon.

faqs.question: Who bears the civil sword?
faqs.answer: Rulers as ministers of God—distinct from the church’s sword of the word.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For he is God’s minister to you for good. But if you do evil, be afraid; for he does not bear the sword in vain; for he is God’s minister, an avenger to execute wrath on him who practices evil.

faqs.question: What must people hear?
faqs.answer: A message of repentance and of righteousness—the word of God that sets free.
